messages:
maya: Quick question — audit export for routing-policy changes currently only has a freeform `diff` field. customers who ship to SIEMs keep asking for structured fields: policy_id, target_route, quota_bucket, and rollout_id. Do we have a plan to add these?

sam: We talked about this in the last sync. I sketched an NDJSON schema that includes `actor_id`, `actor_email`, `resource_type`, `resource_id`, and `change_type` (update/create/delete). But we didn't land on where `quota_bucket` should live — top-level vs inside metadata.

rory: I think `quota_bucket` belongs on the policy object snapshot (so top-level in the exported event) because downstream consumers join on policy id. Also we should include `route_hash` for quick joins when route names change.

maya: +1 on route_hash. Another ask: when a canary rollout happens, we need to know who triggered it and what percentage was targeted. customers want to reconstruct "who changed what and when" for compliance.

aisha: From security/compliance: please include `justification` (free text), `approval_refs` (list of approval ticket ids), and an explicit `pii_redaction_level` enum. We must not export raw emails by default — export should have `actor_email` as hashed unless tenant opts in.

sam: Good catch. We should default to hashed actor identifiers, and add `actor_email_plain` only when `export_mode=full_with_pii`. Need clear doc and checkbox in the console.

rory: UX/console side — when you click a change in the console timeline, we should show both the before/after snapshots and a tiny inline diff. For exports, do we export both snapshots, or just a canonical `diff`? Export size matters for high-throughput customers.

maya: Proposal: export `diff` + `before_summary` and `after_summary` (small objects), and include a `snapshot_link` that points to the full snapshot in the control plane (signed short-lived URL). That keeps NDJSON rows small but reconstructable.

aisha: That works if the snapshots are access-controlled and TTLed. Also add `redaction_policy_version` so auditors know how PII was handled.

sam: Implementation question: should the NDJSON event include a `policy_change_type` enum with values like `param_update`, `route_swap`, `quota_update`, `rollout_start`, `rollout_end`? That will help SIEM rule authors.

maya: yes — make change_type explicit and machine-friendly.

export-bot: sample event (NDJSON) below — baseline idea, not final:
```
{"ts":"1714012345","actor_id":"u_0x1a","actor_email":"sha256:...","change_type":"rollout_start","policy_id":"pol_789","route_hash":"r_3f2","quota_bucket":"gold","rollout_id":"rl_2024_11","rollout_pct":10,"before_summary":{"routes":2,"rules":5},"after_summary":{"routes":3,"rules":6},"diff":"+ route /payments -> backend-v2","snapshot_link":"https://redwood.example/snap/abcd?exp=1714016000","pii_redaction_level":"hashed","redaction_policy_version":"v2"}
```

rory: This is solid. A couple of operational bits: add `export_batch_id` and `sequence_in_batch` for ordering guarantees, and `tenant_id` for multi-tenant joins.

aisha: Also include `retention_days` on the export object (so downstream can enforce retention SLAs). And log the KMS key id used for snapshot encryption as `snapshot_kms_key` (helps audits).

sam: Will spin up a quick PR to the audit-export schema repo. Plan: iterate with a small set of customers on a Canary export stream (ndjson) — include a checkbox in the export UI: "Include plain-actor-email (PII)" with a warning triage.

maya: Action items: Sam to open schema PR + sample consumer mapping, Rory to prototype console diff + snapshot link behavior, Aisha to write the redaction/PII policy text for the export docs. We'll run a two-week canary.

rory: one more edgecase — policy renames: if `policy_id` is stable, that's fine. but if we ever change IDs, include `policy_aliases` array in the export.

maya: noted. thanks all. :thumbsup:
